subject.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64

question: Should a configured image-understanding failure intentionally return only a text notice and explicit share path, or must OpenClaw preserve a non-session-persistent way for the primary model to receive that screenshot?
rationale: The patch fixes a severe session-state failure, but it removes an existing recovery behavior for configured-vision users; repository policy treats fallback removal as an upgrade-sensitive product contract rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve text-only configured-failure recovery
options.body: Accept the branch’s scoped contract: configured vision errors return text and a share hint, while unconfigured/skipped vision retains raw image delivery.

options.title: Require a non-persistent image recovery path
options.body: Keep a usable screenshot recovery path for configured-vision errors, but ensure it cannot store a base64 image block in tool-result session history.

options.title: Pause this behavior change
options.body: Do not merge until the desired recovery contract is settled, leaving the existing fallback in place temporarily.

recommendation.title: Approve text-only configured-failure recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the branch’s scoped contract: configured vision errors return text and a share hint, while unconfigured/skipped vision retains raw image delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current proposed behavior and documented the two recovery options, although a browser-area owner should make the final product decision.
